resources.string: Inverts the page so the mushaf is light text on dark.
Mirrors the recitation and passage screens for Arabic. Word order and the ayah gutter follow.
The horizon on the recitation screen moves continuously. Turn off for a still image.
A short buzz the first time each word is marked wrong in a session, so the verdict reaches you when your eyes are on the page. Unheard words and engine notes never vibrate.

Holds the screen awake everywhere in the app, reciting included. A recitation usually runs past the ~30 s before Android dims the screen, and a screen that goes dark mid-ayah looks like the session ended. Turn off to save battery.
9,706 of 51,395 madd sites are free choice, where Hafs permits more than one length. The engine holds only the canonical one.
The expected text is one realisation: waqf at each ayah end, continuing inside. The mushaf has 9,950 mid-ayah stop marks. Stopping is legal and read as a mismatch.
A word-final sound merges into the next word. Where the engine cannot separate them, no verdict is given.
The exception lists for these are not in any data asset. Those words cannot be judged.
Holding a madd for 2, 4 or 6 counts where more than one is legal is never an error.
Pausing where the text shows a stop mark is a legal recitation choice, not a mistake.
First ayah with nothing before it
When no previous ayah anchors the window, the audio in front may be someone else\'s; the engine cannot prove it is yours, so it is not accused.
What the engine may tell you
What counts as an engine note
Evidence needed before a word can be called wrong
A word must have %1$d%% of its own sounds heard before a mismatch counts against you. Lower means more warnings.
Show engine state in the session report: whether the audio window is healthy, and when the decoder stalled. Silence on screen is not a diagnosis.
The first play streams while the file saves in the background, so replays read the local copy instead of downloading the surah again.
Playback always streams regardless; this only holds back the saved copy while on mobile data.
Saving is off, so the Wi-Fi rule has nothing to apply to. Turn on \"Keep a copy for replay\" to save downloads.
Play the next surah when one ends
Al-Faatiha rolls into Al-Baqarah instead of stopping at the last ayah.
When the count is passed, the oldest sessions and their audio are deleted for good. Statistics built from them stay forever.
Keep the audio of each session

While you recite, the session\'s own sound is written next to its record, so the report can play what the model heard. It never leaves this device and is deleted with its session. Turn off to keep records without audio.
Session audio on disk: %1$s across 1 recording.
Session audio on disk: %1$s across %2$d recordings.
Nothing you recite leaves the device. There is no account, no server and no network access at runtime.
This deletes the %1$d recorded sessions and the statistics built from them. It cannot be undone.
Page images and data are downloaded once and kept in a shared folder, so app updates stay small. The recitation model is supplied by you, once.
model.int8.onnx is gated by its authors, so it cannot be downloaded automatically. Copy it over USB into:\n%1$s\nthen press Re-check.
Continue unlocks once every file is present.
Nothing saved yet. Press play on a surah and the audio saves itself here, so replaying it never downloads it a second time.
%1$s will be removed. Playing the surah again will stream it and save a fresh copy.
1 surah by other reciters (%1$s) will be removed. They stream again if played later.
%1$d surahs by other reciters (%2$s) will be removed. They stream again if played later.
%1$s will be removed. A surah played afterwards streams and saves again.
